lines.say: Do you have to be sore to grow?
Soreness mostly shows up when something is new: a new exercise, more reps, or lots of slow lowering.
Do the same workout again, and soreness fades fast. That's called the repeated bout effect.
But growth keeps going even when you stop getting sore. In studies, soreness and growth don't line up well.
Being wrecked for days can even hurt your next workouts.
Verdict: myth. Track your weights and reps instead. If they go up, you're growing.
A little soreness is fine. It's just not the goal.
